deep.reconstruction:
This page contains no mathematics. It is a fair-copy page of lecture notes on ancient history, continuing from folio 24. The handwriting is a neat German Kurrent and does not look like Gauss's hand; it may be a student's or family member's lecture notebook bound into the bundle. The content is in three parts.

(1) End of 'A. Geschichte des Reichs Israel (975–722)'. Samaria becomes the capital, continuing the previous page's sentence 'Jetzt wurde [es] Samarien'. Under Menahem the dynasty falls into foreign tributary dependence (Assyria). The last king is Hosea (Hoshea): by the time he came to power the kingdom was already in decay, and the inhabitants were deported as captives to Media and Armenia.

(2) 'B. Geschichte des Reichs Juda (975–588)'. Twenty kings and one queen (Athaliah) ruled, beginning with 1) Rehabeam (Rehoboam). Under Jojachin (Jehoiachin) the Jews tried to free themselves from Nebuchadnezzar. They suffered the fate that inhabitants and king had to leave the country (dated 595). Zedekiah was set as king over those who remained. In 588 Jerusalem was taken after a two-year siege.

(3) Start of 'VI. Afrikanische Völker'. Africa has always been the continent that remained most a riddle. In antiquity it was known in part; nevertheless geographical knowledge of it existed even in earlier times.

No derivation, computation, or mathematical problem is present. The only numbers are historical dates in the old Ussher-style chronology: 975, 722, 595 and 588 BC, and the count of 20 kings plus 1 queen.
errors: No mathematical errors, since there is no mathematics.

Historical dates follow the older chronology. Modern dating puts the division of the kingdom at c. 931/930 BC, Jehoiachin's deportation in 597 BC, and the fall of Jerusalem in 587/586 BC. These are period conventions, not slips.
The revolt against Nebuchadnezzar began under Jehoiakim; Jehoiachin reigned only briefly before being deported. The notes compress this.
'Medien und Armenien' as the destination of the deportees: 2 Kings 17:6 names Halah, Habor and the cities of the Medes. 'Armenia' reflects contemporary textbook usage.

transcription_corrections: Line 1 begins 'ed Samarien' (i.e. 'es Samarien', continuing 'Jetzt wurde es Samarien' from p. 24), not 'd. Samaria'. 'Samarien' is underlined.
'Hosea' and 'Rehabeam' are underlined in the manuscript; 'Jojachin' is also underlined.
'Afrika ist von jeher der Welttheil gewesen der am mehrsten ein Räthsel blieb' is confirmed.
'Schon im Alterthume war es einem Theil nach bekannt' — read 'einem' rather than 'seinem'.

'das Schicksal das Israeli-' is probably 'das Schicksal, daß die' / 'der Israeli[tischen]' followed by 'Einwohner mit ihrem König das Vaterland verlassen mußten'. The reading is uncertain but the sense is clear.
The folio number '25' appears faintly in the top right corner.
The catchword 'Afric' or similar appears at the bottom right, linking to p. 26 ('Durch die Karthaginenser...').
